subject: Typewriter
title: Descent of the typewriter
question: How did a printing piano learn to shift, take power from a motor, and trade its hammers for a ball?

ancestors.title: improvement in type-writing machines
ancestors.name: Sholes, Glidden & Soule type-writer
ancestors.trait: A ring of type-bars that all strike one central point, worked by a piano-style row of keys
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1, 5, 7 and text: annular disk B with type-bars o pivoted in radial slots, 'so each type on the inner ends ... will strike against the central point'; keys L 'similar to the key-board of a piano'; anvil O' and platen G on arm D; carriage frames C and E; bar F with pins e.

ancestors.title: improvement in type-writing machines
ancestors.name: Brooks shifting-platen type-writer
ancestors.trait: One key, two letters: each type-bar carries a capital and a small letter, and a handle shifts the platen frame between them
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1, 2 and text: cylindrical platen B in sliding frame C; handle H and spiral spring I; 'when the capitals are required, the roller is simply drawn forward'; type-bars D under frame A; keys E.

ancestors.title: type-writing machine
ancestors.name: Smathers power type-writer
ancestors.trait: Power: a motor-driven roller throws the type-bars, so every key strikes with the same force
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1 and text: driven roller 1 'adapted for rotation by a motor', elliptic wheels 2 (one per key) with links 7, 8 and bar 9; key levers 19, type-bar 18 on link 16, fulcrum 17, lever 20; object: 'power-driven means for operating the type bars'.

ancestors.title: selection mechanism for a single printing element typewriter
ancestors.name: IBM single-element typewriter
ancestors.trait: No type-bars: a single printing element, tilted and turned, travels along a fixed platen
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1, 2: single printing element 10 on shaft 15 of carrier 38, sliding on rails 243 and 218 in front of platen 36; selection mechanism in frame 106 with shaft 92, pulley 90 and latches 141-144.
